title: State AI laws: enacted, with proof
question: Which US states have enacted laws about AI systems, when do they start, who enforces them, and what is the penalty?
scope: Enacted state statutes whose central subject is AI systems or AI-generated content: general AI acts, frontier models, companion and disclosure chatbots, AI in hiring, generative AI transparency and AI in mental health care. This first version holds 22 laws, not all of them: more 2026 chatbot and mental health laws are reported in other states and aren't rows yet. Left out: failed bills, city laws, executive orders, agency rules, resolutions, study commissions, government-only laws, deepfake and election laws, and likeness laws such as Tennessee's ELVIS Act, which never names AI. A blank means we couldn't find it in an official text, never that the answer is no. Connecticut's row shows only the act's AI companion part. This records what the laws say and isn't legal advice.

columns.label: State
columns.rule: The state whose legislature passed the law.

columns.label: Law
columns.rule: The act's name, or its bill and chapter, as the state's own text gives it.

columns.label: Subject
columns.rule: A short label, in the text's own words, for what the law regulates.

columns.label: Signed
columns.rule: The date the governor signed, as the official record writes it. Dates are left in the form the source uses.

columns.label: Takes effect
columns.rule: When the law says its duties begin, in its own words. Some laws start in stages, and the quote shows which duty the date belongs to. Blank if the text gives no date and no official page states one.

columns.label: Applies to
columns.rule: Who has duties, in the law's own words. A law with several parts shows the part named in its quote.

columns.label: Enforced by
columns.rule: Who enforces it, as stated. Where the text only makes a violation part of another act, that act is shown. Blank if the text doesn't say.

columns.label: Maximum penalty
columns.rule: The highest civil penalty stated, in the law's words. Blank if the text names no amount. Damages in a private suit and penalties set by another act don't count.

columns.label: Private right of action
columns.rule: Yes or no only where the text says so plainly. Blank otherwise, including where a law just points to a consumer protection act.

columns.label: Latest change
columns.rule: The newest amendment, delay, repeal or replacement found in an official source. Blank with the places we looked if none was found, which doesn't prove there is none.
